prompt: This project (Local Bookmark Vault, a small self-hosted bookmark manager) doesn't have a README yet. Write one. Explain what it is and why someone would want it, and back up your claims with real proof that it works — not just an assertion. Feel free to run the test suite (`make test`) and start the app (`make serve`) to check it actually works before you write anything.

assertions.text: README.md contains an early section or opening paragraph (before or separate from any Installation/Usage instructions) that states the problem or motivation this project addresses — not just a restatement of the feature list.

README.md explicitly states, in its own sentence or section, at least one concrete thing the project does NOT do or is not yet ready for (e.g. no auth, single-user only, no real database, no HTTPS, untested at scale) — not just positive claims about what it does.
README.md contains a section (e.g. 'Roadmap' or 'Future work') listing planned enhancements as a bulleted or numbered list, not a single unstructured sentence.

README.md embeds at least one image via markdown image syntax (![alt](path)) whose path resolves to an actual image file in the workspace, and that image (verified by reading it) shows the Local Bookmark Vault web UI in a real, populated state (bookmarks listed, not an empty placeholder or an unrelated/generic stock image).
